maml:description.maml:para: Finds access control entries in Active Directory that grant rights to principals that no longer exist.

Walks every object under one or more search bases, reads each security descriptor, resolves every identity reference, and reports the ones that cannot be resolved. Nothing is changed.
Each orphaned access control entry is written to the pipeline as an OrphanedSIDResult with the object's distinguished name, the unresolvable SID, the rights it still grants, and an analysis of where the SID probably came from. The same rows are written to -OutputPath as CSV when that parameter is given. A summary (objects processed, orphaned SIDs found, duration, peak memory) goes to the console and the log.
Results stream to batch files in the temp directory while the run is in progress so memory stays flat on large OUs; the files are removed when the command finishes unless -PreserveTempFiles is set.
JSON configuration file. Only WellKnownSIDPatterns, ProtectedSIDs, BatchSize, MemoryCheckInterval, EnableDetailedLogging, LogLevel, LogFilePath, EnableLogFileRotation and MaxLogFileSizeMB are read.
Identifier carried through every log line and result row. Generated when omitted.
Also report access control entries inherited from parent containers. More rows and a longer run; by default only explicit entries are reported.
Lowest level written to the log file. Security events are written at every level.
Log file. Defaults to .\Logs\Find-OrphanedSid_<yyyyMMdd_HHmmss>.log under the current directory.
Working-set threshold in megabytes at which garbage collection is forced. Default 1024.
Retry attempts for a transient Active Directory failure on one object. Default 3.
CSV file to write the results to, in addition to the pipeline. The parent folder must exist.
Keep the streaming batch files under $env:TEMP\Find-UnknownSID-<CorrelationId>\ for inspection after the run.
Distinguished name of one or more containers to search. Accepts pipeline input. Defaults to the current domain root when omitted.
Write progress and the summary to the log file only.
Distinguished names, by value or by the `DistinguishedName` property of a piped object such as the output of `Get-ADOrganizationalUnit` or `Get-ADObject`.

One object per orphaned access control entry, with `ObjectDN`, `ObjectClass`, `OrphanedSID`, `LikelySource`, `Confidence`, `AnalysisNotes`, `AccessControlType`, `ActiveDirectoryRights`, `InheritanceType`, `ObjectType`, `InheritedObjectType`, `IsInherited`, `ProcessingMethod`, `ActionTaken`, `CorrelationId` and `Timestamp`.

maml:description.maml:para: Removes orphaned access control entries from Active Directory objects after backing up each ACL.

Runs the same discovery as Find-OrphanedSid and then, for every object that carries an orphaned entry, validates each SID against the protected and well-known SID lists, writes a Clixml backup of the object's ACL, and removes the orphaned entries. The backup for a run lands in a timestamped folder so a whole run can be undone with Restore-OrphanedSidBackup.
The command has ConfirmImpact High: it asks once before changing anything. -WhatIf previews the run, listing the entries that would be removed, and creates no backup. An unattended run (scheduled task, CI) cannot answer the prompt and must pass -Force or -Confirm:$false.
Each removal is written to the pipeline as a RemovalOperationResult; -OutputPath writes the discovered entries as CSV.
Folder that receives the per-run backup subfolder. Defaults to .\Backup under the current directory. The parent folder must exist; the backup folder itself is created.
JSON configuration file; see Find-OrphanedSid for the keys read. ProtectedSIDs and WellKnownSIDPatterns are the ones that matter here.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
Identifier carried through every log line, backup file and result. Generated when omitted.
Proceed without the confirmation prompt. Required for unattended runs. -WhatIf still wins.
Also evaluate inherited access control entries. Inherited entries cannot be removed from the child object; they are reported and the parent is where the cleanup belongs.
Lowest level written to the log file. Security events are written at every level.
Log file. Defaults to .\Logs\Remove-OrphanedSid_<yyyyMMdd_HHmmss>.log.
Working-set threshold in megabytes at which garbage collection is forced. Default 1024.
Retry attempts for a transient Active Directory failure on one object. Default 3.
CSV file for the discovered entries. The parent folder must exist.
Keep the streaming batch files after the run.
Distinguished name of one or more containers to clean. Accepts pipeline input. Defaults to the current domain root when omitted.
Write progress and the summary to the log file only.
Runs the command in a mode that only reports what would happen without performing the actions.
Distinguished names, by value or by the `DistinguishedName` property of a piped object such as the output of `Get-ADOrganizationalUnit` or `Get-ADObject`.

One object per Active Directory object whose ACL was modified, with the object DN, the SIDs that were intended for removal and the ones actually removed, the backup file written, the verification outcome, any error, and the correlation ID.

maml:description.maml:para: Restores Active Directory ACLs from a backup folder written by Remove-OrphanedSid.

Reads the Clixml backup files in -BackupPath, validates each one (format, object DN, SDDL and its SHA256 hash), applies the saved security descriptor to the object, and reads the ACL back to verify the result.
-TargetObjectDN decides the scope. A container (an OU or the domain root) restores every backup whose object sits under it. A single object restores its most recent matching backup. -BackupPath is the folder that holds the .xml files, normally one timestamped run folder under the Remove-OrphanedSid backup root.
The command has ConfirmImpact High: it asks once before writing anything. -WhatIf previews the restore. An unattended run must pass -Force or -Confirm:$false.
One result object per restored object is written to the pipeline; -OutputPath writes the same rows as CSV.
Folder containing the backup .xml files. Must exist.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
Identifier carried through every log line and result. Generated when omitted.
Proceed without the confirmation prompt. Required for unattended runs.
Lowest level written to the log file. Security events are written at every level.
Log file. Defaults to .\Logs\Restore-OrphanedSidBackup_<yyyyMMdd_HHmmss>.log.
CSV file for the restore results. The parent folder must exist.
Write progress and the summary to the log file only.
Distinguished name of the object or container to restore. Accepts pipeline input.
Runs the command in a mode that only reports what would happen without performing the actions.
Distinguished names, by value or by the `DistinguishedName` property of a piped object such as the output of `Get-ADOrganizationalUnit` or `Get-ADObject`.

One object per target. For a container it summarises the run (`TotalObjects`, `SuccessfulRestores`, `FailedRestores`, `IndividualResults`); for a single object it is that object's restore result. Both carry `Success`, `TargetObjectDN`, `EntriesRestored`, `ErrorMessage` and `CorrelationId`.
